copies.headline: Noah's Backfield Can't Cover His Everything Else
copies.body:
Noah's roster is two running backs and a prayer. De'Von Achane and James Cook are legitimately the best RB pair in this matchup, and after that it's Garrett Wilson carrying a receiver room where the second-best options are a questionable Mike Evans, a questionable Josh Downs, and Michael Wilson in a game Arizona is losing by ten and a half. Drake Maye in Seattle as a dog and Colston Loveland at tight end is not a plan, it's a shrug. Power ranking #12 for a reason.
John has the Rams stack in a 48.5-point game — Stafford and Puka Nacua, with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum vulturing the same offense. He also gets to bench Trey McBride, a top-five tight end, because Brock Bowers exists. That's the difference: John's worst starting decisions are luxuries, Noah's are triage. If Nacua sits, Brian Thomas Jr. and Quentin Johnston still beat whatever Noah's stapling into flex.

copies.headline: Isaac's Injury Report Is His Depth Chart
copies.body:
Isaac's receiver room looks great until you read the fine print: Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, DK Metcalf, Wan'Dale Robinson and Jakobi Meyers are all questionable, which means his 46-point WR edge is really a coin flip with five sides. Behind that it gets grim. Bo Nix at Arrowhead in a 42.5 total is the QB1, the backup is Malik Willis, and the running backs are Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo and Jaylen Warren — three guys who split touches with somebody. Tight end is Hockenson or Kincaid, both nine points, both boring. Power ranking says 10th of 12 for a reason.
Kaleb isn't clean either — Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall both carry tags, and if they sit, RJ Harvey and a Vikings defense projected for four points are the parachute. But Justin Herbert against Arizona as a 10.5-point favorite is the best quarterback on the field by a mile, Ladd McConkey comes with him, and Drake London plus Harold Fannin give him floor Isaac doesn't have. Healthier where it counts.

copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Is A Hospital Wing
copies.body:
Grant's receiving room actually functions: Amon-Ra St. Brown against a Saints defense in a 49.5 shootout, Waddle, Watson, Godwin, and a questionable Zay Flowers as the fourth or fifth option. That's a 45-to-39 edge at wideout and it's the whole ballgame, because Omarion Hampton gets Arizona with the Chargers laying 10.5 and Grant's RB room has actual bodies behind him. The quarterback thing is a coin flip he's fine losing — Kyler Murray and Baker Mayfield project identically, which is its own kind of insult to Baker.
CJ, meanwhile, is running a triage tent. Pacheco on IR, Charbonnet out, Hubbard and Henderson both questionable, so it's Jonathan Taylor and pray Judkins does something in a 40.5-total game where Cleveland is getting 7.5. The receivers are worse: Rashee Rice, then Egbuka and Pierce with question marks, then Parker Washington. Jake Ferguson at tight end is a shrug. Burrow's +2 doesn't cover any of that.

copies.headline: Logan's Eagles Stack Buries Adam's Committee
copies.body:
Logan opens with the Philly cheat code: Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley both cashing in a game Philly is favored by 4.5, plus Justin Jefferson and Tetairoa McMillan. Yes, the depth chart is a hospital ward — Jeremiyah Love, Pittman, Burden and Stribling all questionable, and Isaiah Likely is the entire tight end room — but the top four score enough to make that irrelevant. Adam's counter is Jayden Daniels getting hunted by that same Eagles defense as a 4.5-point dog, which is a fun way to lose two positions in one game.
Adam's real problem is running back by committee with no committee chairman. Kenneth Walker, Rico Dowdle, Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell all project 11-15, which means four coin flips instead of one answer. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave are legitimately good, and if Sam LaPorta's questionable tag holds, Mark Andrews covers it. Not enough. Logan's top-heavy roster only needs to survive one week, and Week 1 is exactly when top-heavy works.

copies.headline: Peter's Questionable Tags Sink The Basement
copies.body:
Christian's roster is the deeper one and it isn't close in the places that matter. Lamb, DeVonta Smith and Jameson Williams give him three real WR starts, plus Deebo and Shakir rotting on the bench, while Peter is praying Tee Higgins' injury tag flips and that George Pickens plays like a guy who cares in a 48.5-point Giants game. Christian's backfield is a two-headed nothing-special — Chase Brown and Etienne, who's a 7-point dog in Detroit and might get 11 touches — but Peter's is Bijan Robinson at Pittsburgh in a 41.5 total and then a shrug: Jonathon Brooks questionable, Kyle Monangai questionable, Jordan Mason buried behind Aaron Jones' old job.
The tiebreaker is tight end, where Peter owns exactly one: Tucker Kraft, questionable. If Kraft sits, Peter is streaming a zero at the position and Christian still has Chig Okonkwo behind a banged-up Kittle. Lamar over Trevor Lawrence buys back two points. It's not enough to cover the four bodies Peter's missing.

copies.headline: Leif's Injury Ward Beats Mitchell's Jaxson Dart Experiment
copies.body:
Leif's roster is a hospital wing with a Josh Allen wristband: McCaffrey questionable, Mahomes questionable, and a tight end room that begins and ends with Kyle Pitts, the most reliable 10-point disappointment in football. But the backfield is genuinely fat — Henry against Indy, Montgomery, a healthy-enough CMC — and the receiver group has real names even if Adams and Harrison Jr. spend half their weeks running decoy routes.
Mitchell's counter is starting Jaxson Dart, at home, as a 2.5-point dog to Dallas, with Daniel Jones as the panic button. That is not a quarterback room, that's a hostage situation. Gibbs is a monster and Nico Collins is legit, but behind them it's Josh Jacobs at zero, Kaleb Johnson at one, Tank Dell on IR, and Rachaad White limping. Two studs and a bake sale. Leif's depth wins a game neither team should be proud of.

intro:
Leif at Mitchell is the game of the week by 0.8 points, which is another way of saying two guys who drafted identical teams are going to spend Sunday screaming at the same waiver-wire tight end. Elsewhere, John is favored by 8.8 over Noah, so Noah gets to open the season by learning what his roster actually is, and Logan gets Adam by 6.8 in a game that looks less like a matchup and more like a scheduled appointment.

Isaac-Kaleb and Christian-Peter are both coin flips nobody will admit to losing on merit, and Grant walks into CJ's place a 2.4-point favorite with the confidence of a man who hasn't checked his kicker's situation yet.
